title: Prompt proactively for human decisions with minimal input

requirement.summary: Replace special confirmation words in the primary human-review path with a vendor-neutral proactive decision prompt that explains the decision, recommends one bounded option, accepts a single structured selection, and records exactly what the human selected without treating display or Coding Agent interpretation as approval.

objective.rationale: Risk routing reduces how often humans are interrupted, but the remaining review path still asks users to remember exact words or manually compose commands. The intended experience keeps decisions human-owned while making the system responsible for presenting the choice and carrying the selected bounded transition forward.

goal: Add strict vendor-neutral decision-prompt and decision-result contracts, proactive single-selection rendering, and a trusted reference selection flow that binds a human choice to the exact prompt and existing Core transition while keeping special confirmation words only as explicit fallback interfaces.
non_goals: Do not infer a decision from free-form user text, silence, Coding Agent output, tool permission, environment variables, command flags, or prompt display alone.
Do not claim a host can render or record native controls when its declared capabilities say context-only or unavailable.
Do not require raw prompts, transcripts, assistant responses, source content, credentials, model identifiers, absolute host paths, or free-text rationale in the decision contracts.
Do not let a decision result expand scope, approve an exception, authorize arbitrary commands, commit, merge, deploy, release, publish, or write to an external system.
Do not automatically approve full-review material work, start or replace a session, or invent a Core event for an option that has no implemented transition.
Do not delete the exact ADMIT, START, REPLACE, or HANDOFF terminal fallbacks in this bounded compatibility slice.
Do not add a hidden daemon, install a host component, add a second vendor Adapter, or claim cryptographic human identity.
acceptance_signals: A strict vendor-neutral decision-prompt contract binds the exact source request and digest, explains why a decision is needed, identifies one recommendation, presents two or more bounded options, requires exactly one selection, and requires no free-text input.

A strict decision-result contract binds the exact prompt and source request digests, records one option selected by a human through a declared trusted host or interactive-terminal attestation, carries only the option's predeclared Core transition, and rejects unknown or authoritative fields.

Prompt display is proactive for real human gates and absent for observe-only, continue-active, and fast-track routes. Codex Hooks continue to report context-only/unavailable custom-decision capability instead of claiming false native support.

The reference presenter renders the complete concise choice before input, accepts a single numeric selection rather than a special confirmation word, does not echo or retain raw input, and records decline or change-request choices without repository writes.

A low-risk human-review route may apply only the exact already-built task admission plan after an approve selection; apply revalidates policy, request, prompt, result, task digest, and exclusive target and creates only that task.
Scope and completion decision results map only to their existing scope.decision_recorded and session.reviewed events; task routing options with no implemented transition remain non-applying guidance.
Existing fast-track, exact ADMIT fallback, task proposal, Coding Agent cards, JSONL, Codex Hook, session, scope, completion, packaging, and repository behavior remains compatible.
Focused tests, the complete Python 3.11 suite, task/scope/repository checks, schema parsing, packaging assertions, and diff checks pass.
validation_commands: python -m unittest tests.test_human_decision tests.test_admission_routing tests.test_host_interaction tests.test_coding_agent_transport tests.test_codex_hooks tests.test_task_contract -v

items: A visually convenient selection could be mistaken for broader authority than the exact option describes.
A Coding Agent could forge a human selection if the Adapter trust boundary and actor source are not explicit.
A prompt or task could drift after presentation so the applied transition differs from the human-reviewed choice.
A host without native decision recording could be misrepresented as providing a trusted one-click approval.

stop_conditions: Stop if displaying a prompt, choosing a recommendation by default, or receiving Coding Agent text can count as a human decision.
Stop if a result is not bound to the exact prompt, source request, option, and predeclared transition reviewed by the human.
Stop if an unavailable/context-only host can produce a result that claims trusted native recording.

Stop if approval can apply material/full-review work, overwrite a target, start a session, execute a command, expand scope, approve an exception, or authorize Git, deployment, release, or publication.
Stop if the primary selection requires an exact magic word or free-text rationale instead of one bounded choice.
Stop before any Git write, host installation, release, consumer mutation, deployment, or external-system write.

decision.rationale: The user reviewed the completed proactive minimal-input decision flow, identified the need for governed multi-turn discussion before options are stable, and explicitly authorized clarification dialogue and drift re-centering on 2026-08-06.
